conventions.convention: Discretization invariance includes specified finite-dimensional sampling and output reconstruction, with convergence in the actual output Banach norm on every compact input set. Point samples of equivalence classes require an explicit representative convention.
The elliptic principal part has positive divergence sign, and div(bu) is summed once, separately from the double principal sum.
The parabolic equation is -u_t+L_tu=f. Prescribed data occupy the initial and lateral faces; the spatial-interior final-time face is excluded.

For d=1, the entire finite boundary contribution is evaluated exactly; there is no random boundary sample or boundary Hölder penalty. A zero regularization coefficient contributes zero even for an infinite seminorm.

The active sampling assumptions hold only at specified small scales. The exact thresholds use the same unnormalized lower-mass constants throughout; no comparability of their two coordinates is assumed.

The printed BA class uses a global output bound C for every C at least the diameter of K, including C=0 for a singleton. The radius-based replacement in the universality theorem is a different property.

The integral universality subclass has N≥2 affine integral stages, exactly N-2 intermediate activations, zero local terms, and a final kernel on the output-domain/input-domain product integrated over the input domain.
Exterior spheres give local interior Hölder regularity and continuous boundary attainment. Global C2alpha regularity requires the separately stated smooth-boundary and lifting hypotheses.
Parabolic energy identification additionally requires the displayed divergence expansion to agree in distributions; pointwise differentiability alone is not silently substituted for that condition.

load_bearing.statement: Under its explicit small-scale partition and ball-mass assumptions, nested iid sampling, exact regularization conditions, finite data/trial Hölder seminorms, and uniformly seminorm-bounded zero-empirical-loss witnesses, every global minimizer has population loss and squared uniform residual errors O(A_r+A_b) on the respective hit-cell and occupancy events. Almost surely both uniform residual errors tend to zero along every count pair tending to infinity. No comparability of the regularization coordinates is required.

Assume Countable Choice. On a bounded Lipschitz open set, each listed W^{m,p} space with finite p, including Lp, and each Cm closure space admits bounded finite-rank linear approximations to the identity uniformly on every norm-compact set, with ambient compactly supported smooth range. Its explicit inward smoothing maps are uniformly bounded and converge compact-uniformly to the identity.

For the specified partition with cell masses at least m^{-1/2}, iid samples populate every cell with at least sqrt(m)/2 observations with probability at least max{0,1-sqrt(m) exp(-sqrt(m)/8)}. On that event the displayed uniform residual inequality holds simultaneously for every pair of functions with finite Hölder seminorms, including sample-dependent functions.

Assume AC and Countable Choice and the stated bounded Lipschitz exterior-ball domain, finite global coefficient regularity, symmetry, uniform ellipticity and nonpositive expanded potential. Every globally Hölder forcing and continuous boundary datum has a unique locally C2alpha classical solution continuous on the closure, with the displayed residual stability estimate. Zero boundary data give H1_0 membership and the stated energy bound; the global C2alpha branch requires its additional boundary and lifting hypotheses.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. On the stated bounded open exterior-ball domain, bounded locally parabolic Hölder coefficients and forcing, uniform ellipticity, nonpositive potential, and compatible continuous initial-lateral data give a unique interior classical solution continuous on the closed cylinder, bounded by the data supremum plus T times the forcing supremum. Smooth weak approximants have the stated interior convergence and bounds.

Under its AC, Countable Choice, exterior-ball, bounded coefficient, ellipticity, local Hölder and distributionally compatible expansion hypotheses, every bounded locally classical continuous zero-initial-lateral solution with the stated residual belongs to the zero-boundary evolution energy space and is its unique variational solution, with the displayed energy estimate.

Compact-uniform convergence H_n→H between the stated Banach spaces is preserved after continuous finite-dimensional input reconstructions converging compact-uniformly in the actual input norm. The explicit normalized tag weights supply such reconstructions for continuous inputs in the supremum norm. An integral-only first input stage already factors through its finite sample vector under the stated compatibility assumptions.

Under AC and Countable Choice, already smooth zero-boundary solutions on the stated smooth-domain family satisfy a uniform global C2alpha a priori estimate using only the displayed geometric and coefficient controls. Every bounded C2alpha domain has relatively compact smooth approximating open sets with those uniform atlas controls and eventual containment of each interior compact set.

concerns.concern: The Definition requires density in 'C^m(K) in the C^m norm' for every compact K⊂R^q, but does not define this space or norm when m>0 and K has empty interior. Values on K alone do not determine derivatives; for K={0}, the zero function and x↦x have the same restriction and different first derivatives. Specify the ambient-function/jet convention used by this density premise. The universality proof needs derivative approximation of ambient smooth targets on the output closure.

The Definition starts with a continuous torus field but describes b_t only as 'a real bias function' and says only that sigma acts coordinatewise. It does not explicitly retain continuity and periodicity conditions ensuring that the displayed result is again a continuous torus field, as required by the cited neural-operator architecture. For example, W=R=0, identity activation and a discontinuous bias produce a discontinuous output. State the inherited admissibility conditions explicitly.

Proof 1.1 applies classical residual stability to h_m-u*, and Proof 2.1 explicitly asserts that this error belongs to C2(U)∩C(cl U). The Statement imports the regularized-loss theorem's trial-class assumptions, whose displayed C^{k,alpha} condition leaves k unspecified, rather than explicitly requiring classical C2 trial functions. Bind that classical-trial requirement so the stability supplier's regularity hypothesis is stated.

Proofs 1.1–2.1 use classical parabolic stability and classical-to-energy identification for h_m-u*. The Statement imports the sampling theorem's trial-class assumptions without explicitly saying that every admitted h_m is C^{2,1}(Q) and continuous on the closed cylinder. Make this regularity premise explicit; finite Hölder seminorms of the evaluated residual and boundary restriction alone are the sampling theorem's operative assumptions.
